# Myto

> Myto is a local-first AI coding workspace. It reads your project, uses the tools you approve, and helps carry work through implementation and verification.

## Primary pages

- Product page: /
- Download page: /download — the platform chooser; every "Download" control on the site leads here
- Chat: /chat — a live, model-backed chat for Myto, styled like a full chat app; ask a question and it streams an answer. Backed by a same-origin server gateway with a free per-visitor token budget.
- Machine-readable guide: /llms.txt

## Product facts

- Platform: Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and Android are supported today. A browser build is available at https://mytocode.vercel.app.
- Current release: v0.9.0 — a Windows installer (Myto-Setup.exe) and a native Android APK (myto.apk) ship together from GitHub Releases.
- Price: the app is free; the only cost is whatever model provider you choose to use.
- Privacy: Myto is local-first — it works from your project on your machine, with the integrations you configure.
- Models: a local Ollama endpoint (http://localhost:11434 by default) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in Settings. Reasoning effort is a per-turn setting from low to max.
- Core workflow: understand the repository, plan, use approved tools, edit, and verify the build.
- Approvals: reads run automatically, edits are shown as a diff before they are written, and commands, network access, and destructive steps ask first. Permission modes are ask-every-time, auto-approve-edits, and autonomous.
- Extensibility: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and Markdown Skills extend the workspace; slash commands and plugins are available in the chat.
- Also included: a real terminal, a live dev-server preview it can inspect, the Mytorium browser, sub-agents with git-worktree isolation, background runs, MYTO.md project memory, hooks and scheduled tasks, image input, and a headless CLI (`myto -p "<prompt>"`, with `--json`).

## Page map

The product page is a single main landmark with labelled sections. Read the headings in DOM order:

1. Build with your tools still in reach — the hero: what Myto is, an example turn, four facts at a glance, plus Download and "try in browser".
2. A look inside — three screenshots of the app: the diff-first chat, the built-in Mytorium browser, and permission-gated connectors.
3. What it does — capabilities grouped as Understand, Plan & edit, Use tools, Verify, Work in parallel, and Automate.
4. Everything in one window — a flat list of the workspace surface, from diffs and the terminal to memory, automation, and headless mode.
5. Questions — answers on privacy, model choice, approvals, cost, platforms, and offline use.
6. Install — download for Windows, four steps to a first task, what you need, the headless invocation, and the self-signed note.

The download page (/download) is a separate document with its own heading, "Download Myto", then one block per platform under #platforms:

- Windows — Available now. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Direct link to the Myto-Setup.exe installer. Self-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run (More info → Run anyway).
- Android — Available now. Recent Android phones and tablets. Direct link to the myto.apk build. Self-signed, so Android asks you to allow the install the first time.

The chat (/chat) is a separate document styled like a full chat app — a left sidebar (Myto, then New chat, Code, Projects, Artifacts, Customize) beside a main column that opens on a time-of-day greeting over one input, then becomes a transcript once a message is sent. It is a live, streaming chat, and it is bring-your-own-key: after signing in, the user adds their own OpenAI-compatible base URL, API key, and models on the Authentication page (stored to their account), and those models power the chat here and in the desktop and mobile apps. A visitor's messages are sent to a same-origin server gateway (/api/chat) that proxies to the user's own endpoint and streams the reply back token by token; replies render as Markdown. If the endpoint is unreachable it falls back to a built-in knowledge base so the page still answers. It answers questions about Myto itself; everything it states is also on the product page and in this file.

## Reading guidance

- All content is present in the initial document. Sections fade in on scroll, but that is a CSS opacity change only — nothing is loaded, injected, or gated behind it.
- Stable anchors: #top (hero), #inside (screenshots), #features (what it does), #workspace (everything in one window), #faq (questions), #install (download and steps). On /download: #top and #platforms. On /chat: #chat-input (the message box); that page has its own app-style sidebar instead of the site header and footer.
- The FAQ answers are always expanded; there is nothing to click open.
- Screenshots in "A look inside" are real captures of the app; their alt text describes each one, and the sample project shown in them is illustrative.
- The Download controls are supplementary; both pages read without operating them. Every one of them navigates to /download, except the direct installer link on /download itself.
